description:
Nvidia shares have soared following the news that Jensen Huang has returned as CEO - the tech boss had stepped down earlier this month after admitting an affair with a woman who was alleged to be a Chinese spy. 

Adam is joined by economics editor Faisal Islam to assess who or what is behind Huang’s reinstatement.  

Also, COP31, the UN climate change conference which took place in Turkey, has finished with a failure to reach an agreement due to divisions over fossil fuel and money. 

To discuss what went wrong Adam is joined by climate editor Justin Rowlett who has been at the conference, and Camilla Born CEO of electrify Britain and deputy director of strategy for COP26.

author: BBC News
description:
President Volodymyr Zelensky has confirmed that Ukraine sunk a Russian warship, and struck a Russia-bound cargo ship, in the Mediterranean Sea off the Libyan port of Benghazi. Kyiv has released video of sea drones hitting the ships, causing large explosions. This comes one day after a Russian cargo vessel was struck in the Baltic Sea near Finland.

The is only the latest instance of the war in Ukraine spilling over into other territories. Poland has said Russian missiles entered its airspace last week - a development that Nato chief Mark Rutte called "a grave violation". 

In this video we look at the global spread of the war in Ukraine, and ask why Russia has a military presence in North Africa. Plus, our analyst tells us how these latest attacks could be read as a message to Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump, after the two leaders' trilateral summit with Xi Jinping of China.

02:48 Is Russia more vulnerable to Ukraine
title: Why Ukraine's war with Putin is going global, as Russian ship sinks off Libya | Global News Podcast

author: BBC News
description:
On Thursday, 19th November, the International Court of Justice found Myanmar guilty of committing genocide against the Rohingya minority.

The case concerns the 2017 attacks on Rohingya people by Myanmar’s military, in which thousands of Rohingya were killed and more 700,000 were forced to flee to neighbouring Bangladesh. 

The ICJ ruling marks the first time a state has ever been found guilty of genocide by an international court. 

The Global Story's Asma Khalid speaks to Philippe Sands KC, one of the key lawyers involved in the landmark case, to understand what it takes to prove a genocide – and what this ruling could mean for the future of international law.

Jensen Huang has been reinstated as the CEO and president of Nvidia, its board says.
 
He stepped down earlier this month, after admitting an affair with a woman who was alleged to be a Chinese spy - he was also accused of an affair with an Nvidia executive.
 
But the Nvidia board has "voted unanimously" to reinstate him, "following a series of discussions and meetings with Mr Huang, after which the board was satisfied with respect to Mr Huang's candor and ability to lead Nvidia", the company says.
 
Huang says, "I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment".

author: BBC News
description:
Thousands of people were evacuated from a concert in Manchester after an "unknown substance" was released into the crowd.
 
It happened towards the end of US rapper Don Toliver's show at the Co-op Live arena at about 22:00 GMT on Sunday, with music fans describing a "horrible smell" and people "screaming".
 
One person was taken to hospital while more than 50 people were assessed for "eye and respiratory symptoms", the North West Ambulance Service said.
 
Greater Manchester Police (GMP) said a major incident was declared after reports of people suffering from the effects of an unknown substance, which police initially believed to be tear gas.
 
Police said 12,000 people had been evacuated and one fan told of "distressing scenes" with people "choking" as they left.

The streets of France have been rocked by protests and violence in recent weeks.

Demonstrations by students demanding better conditions have been joined by yellow vest activists and others, angry about the rising cost of living.

Images of young, masked protesters dressed in black, clashing with police and smashing up shop windows, have made headlines around the world.

President Macron has blamed the violence on the radical left. But who are these protesters? What drives them to use violence? And what are they really fighting for?

Our Europe Editor Katya Adler investigates.

author: BBC News
description:
The Democratic Party has won the largest majority in the US House of Representatives since 1992, after Democrat Chuck Hubbard unseated Republican Representative Virginia Foxx in North Carolina.
 
The race was called on Sunday, with Hubbard beating Foxx by 330 votes with 99% counted. It was one of the closest contests of the recent midterm elections, in which Democrats also secured the Senate.
 
The party has now won at least 258 House seats in the midterms compared to Republicans, who hold at least 173 seats, with four races still yet to be called.
 
Neither party had won as many House races since 1992, when Bill Clinton won the presidency and Democrats won a total of 258 seats.
